content:
iPhone Ultra will debut at the just-confirmed September 9 launch event. Apple's foldable phone arrives a full seven years later than rivals, but the iPhone Ultra's three key selling points make the wait worthwhile. Here are the upcoming features to look out for.

#1: Near Crease-Free Display

Samsung launched its first foldable phone back in 2019, a full seven years before the iPhone Ultra. However, rumors suggest one of Apple's goals in developing a foldable is to eliminate any visible crease on the display.

A visible crease on the inner display has always been a design trade-off for foldable phones. But all signs point to Apple successfully delivering a near crease-free display.

According to leakers, a very faint crease may still be visible under certain angles and lighting conditions; but overall, we expect the unfolded inner display to look essentially crease-free.

#2: Ultra-Thin Design Without Sacrificing Battery Life or Performance

If a foldable phone isn't slim enough, it ends up feeling bulky; but achieving an ultra-thin design often means compromising on battery life, performance and thermal management.

However, rumors suggest last year's iPhone Air was a stepping stone towards an ultra-thin foldable, while still delivering solid battery life and performance.

The iPhone Ultra is not expected to match the battery life of the iPhone 18 Pro Max, but its physical battery specs combined with efficiency gains from the A20 Pro and C2 chips should still provide sufficient endurance.

In addition, the A20 Pro paired with a vapor chamber design is expected to deliver excellent performance.

#3: Durable Hinge Built on Technology Developed for Over 15 Years

According to reports, the iPhone Ultra's hinge will use liquid metal, a technology Apple licensed more than 15 years ago.

As far back as the early 2010s, there were widespread predictions that liquid metal would help make iPhones thinner and lighter. Back in 2010, there were even mentions of this technology helping Apple develop a foldable phone.

Now we may finally see liquid metal technology put to good use. Reports suggest this will help Apple create a durable and smooth hinge that can withstand long-term, frequent use.

Apple could absolutely have launched a foldable iPhone much sooner, but the timing finally seems right to produce a foldable worthy of the iPhone name.
